definitionEn: to severely restrict the scope or freedom of an action

definitionEn: coming after something in time; following
exampleSentence: The initial trial produced weak results, but subsequent studies confirmed the effect.

definitionEn: suggested or understood without being directly stated

definitionEn: to make an action or process easier

definitionEn: based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system
exampleSentence: The committee's decision seemed arbitrary, with no documented criteria behind it.

definitionEn: open to more than one interpretation; not clearly defined
exampleSentence: The instructions were ambiguous, so several teams interpreted the task differently.

definitionHe: לכיד ועקבי; הגיוני ומובנה מבחינה פנימית
definitionEn: logical and consistent; forming a unified whole
exampleSentence: The author presents a coherent argument that builds logically from one paragraph to the next.

definitionEn: available as another possibility or choice
exampleSentence: Researchers proposed an alternative explanation for the sudden temperature drop.

definitionEn: a fact or condition connected with an event, often beyond one's control
exampleSentence: Under no circumstance should the sample be exposed to direct sunlight.

definitionEn: a remark expressing an opinion or reaction, or a written note of explanation
exampleSentence: The editor added a comment questioning the author's use of the term.

definitionEn: to give something, typically money, in recognition of loss or damage, or to counterbalance an effect
exampleSentence: The airline agreed to compensate passengers for the extended delay.

definitionEn: a part or element of a larger whole, especially a machine or system
exampleSentence: Each component of the engine was tested separately before final assembly.

definitionEn: permission for something to happen, given voluntarily by a competent person
exampleSentence: Participants signed a form giving their informed consent before the procedure began.

definitionEn: notably large in size, amount, or extent
exampleSentence: The renovation required a considerable investment of both time and money.

definitionEn: occurring continuously over time; not changing
exampleSentence: The experiment held temperature constant while pressure varied.

definitionEn: to give something, especially money or time, to help achieve a goal, or to be a factor in a result
exampleSentence: Poor ventilation likely contributed to the spread of the illness.

definitionEn: an agreed rule or method, or a formal meeting of members of a group
exampleSentence: Academic convention requires every quotation to be cited in full.

definitionEn: the central or most important part of something
exampleSentence: The core argument of the essay rests on a single disputed statistic.

definitionEn: to match or be equivalent to something, or to communicate by exchanging letters
exampleSentence: Each bar in the chart corresponds to a single household surveyed.

definitionEn: principles or standards by which something may be judged or decided
exampleSentence: The scholarship committee published its selection criteria in advance.

definitionEn: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from general principles or known facts
exampleSentence: From the fossil's jaw shape, paleontologists deduced its likely diet.

definitionEn: to clearly show the existence or truth of something by giving proof or evidence
exampleSentence: The pilot study demonstrated that the shorter protocol was equally effective.

definitionEn: a piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence
exampleSentence: The historian located an original document confirming the treaty's date.

definitionEn: to have a controlling influence over something, or to be the most noticeable feature
exampleSentence: A single supplier came to dominate the regional market within a decade.

definitionEn: special importance or prominence given to something
exampleSentence: The revised curriculum places greater emphasis on written argumentation.

definitionEn: to make certain that something will happen or be the case

definitionEn: to deny someone access to a place, group, or privilege, or to leave something out of consideration

definitionEn: an essential supporting structure, or a set of ideas used as a basis for judgment
exampleSentence: The paper adopts a theoretical framework borrowed from behavioral economics.

definitionEn: to explain or make clear by using examples, or to provide pictures for a text
exampleSentence: The following case illustrates how small design choices affect user behavior.

definitionEn: to suggest or indicate something indirectly, without stating it explicitly
exampleSentence: The report's cautious tone implies that the authors expect the results to be challenged.

definitionEn: existing or occurring at the beginning

definitionEn: an example or single occurrence of something

definitionEn: to communicate or react with one another, or to have an effect on each other

definitionEn: to show or prove something to be right or reasonable

definitionEn: to make something as large or great as possible

definitionEn: the way a thing turns out; a consequence or result

definitionEn: the study of the fundamental nature of knowledge, reality, and existence

definitionEn: relating to the body or the material world, as opposed to the mind or spirit
exampleSentence: The therapy combines physical exercise with structured breathing techniques.

definitionEn: to prepare and issue a book, journal, or other material for public distribution
exampleSentence: The journal will publish the corrected version in its next issue.

definitionEn: being or happening at the end of a process; fundamental or basic
exampleSentence: The ultimate responsibility for the decision rested with the department head.
